transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-05 10:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Hale (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Evan Kim (Lyra Head of ML), Sofia Martinez (Lyra Platform), Dr. Alan Chu (Lyra Compliance)

Summary (auto): Quick review of week one POC numbers, tuning experiments, and next steps for dedicated benchmarking + compliance docs.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick check-in for week two of the pilot. we've got about 40 minutes. main agenda is numbers, caching, batching and next steps. Evan, Sofia, any new items on your side before we dive in?
[00:16] Evan: nope we're good, uh just curious on the tokens per dollar numbers you mentioned last time, wanted to see the delta after you applied the prefix cache and the quant profile.
[00:24] Priya: yeah so quick recap — baseline on hosted for the llama-2-derived variant (our v2-quant) was roughly 380 tokens/sec/$ under default batching 8, p50 latency ~120ms, p95 ~240ms. after we enabled prefix caching and the light quant path, we saw effective tokens/sec/$ move up to about 790, so roughly a 2x improvement. those are rounded numbers, pipeline noise aside.
[00:48] Sofia: 2x is pretty meaningful. is that mostly cache hits or the quant speedups?
[00:53] Priya: split — prefix caching accounted for about 25% of the delta (so ~475 tokens/sec/$ if you remove quant), quantization path about 30-35% of the remaining improvement, and then batching tweaks filled the rest. important note: prefix caching savings rely on repeated prompt prefixes; for totally fresh sessions it's lower.
[01:12] Evan: that aligns with our traffic — about 40% repeats due to the triage forms. what about KV cache? you mentioned KV savings in the pilot doc.
[01:20] Priya: yes small KV cache — that's more about long-running chat sessions, we measured a further 15-18% compute saving when we could reuse the KV across turns. again, needs session affinity and sticky routing to the same GPU.
[01:35] Jordan: quick practical tradeoff — batching bigger helps tokens/sec/$ but hurts p95 latency. we did a microbenchmark: batch 8 -> batch 32 increased throughput ~2.4x, but p95 latency jumped from ~210ms to ~480ms. for Lyra's triage flow your p95 target was 300ms, right Evan?
[01:55] Evan: yeah ideally sub 300 for user-facing autosuggest, but we can tolerate higher for background summarization. so we need a mixed policy.
[02:03] Sofia: can Redwood do routing by policy? e.g., keep autosuggest on low-latency nodes and background on throughput-optimized?
[02:09] Priya: absolutely — policy routing is available. we can pin autosuggest to a low-batch low-latency pool and route background jobs to a high-batch pool, or use our dynamic fallback if pool saturated. note: more pools = more cost surface.
[02:25] Evan: that makes sense. curious about dedicated vs hosted economics — is the dedicated cluster going to be worth the ops lift?
[02:32] Jordan: based on initial estimates, a small dedicated pool (2x A100-equivalent capacity we used in hosted test) gives ~3x predictable tokens/sec/$ vs hosted at current pricing and removes the multi-tenant noisy neighbor variance. but there's a commit and procurement considerations.
[02:47] Evan: do you have a worked example? like assuming 100k requests/day with median token usage 800 tokens each, what's our monthly spend hosted vs dedicated?
[02:55] Jordan: yes, we'll send a spreadsheet, but high level: hosted (with caching/batching mixed policies) estimated $8k/month; dedicated with reserved capacity and same optimizations ~ $4.5k/month — big caveat is the committed minimum and scaling policy for peak.
[03:14] Dr. Chu: from compliance, we'd like to see KMS integration and audit log retention before we move beyond pilot. is that covered in the private option?
[03:22] Priya: yes — Private and Dedicated support customer-managed KMS and long-term audit logs. we have an onboarding checklist and SOC2 package; Jordan will share the high level doc.
[03:31] Dr. Chu: also curious about data residency — any EU data flows if we use a US host? we might have telemedicine constraints.
[03:38] Jordan: good point — region pinning is available; we can run the pilot in a EU region if you want, we'd just need to coordinate the instance availability and routing latency. Sofia, is that a blocker?
[03:47] Sofia: we can try EU for the next run, but network egress costs are a factor. I'll pull our constraints into the worksheet.
[03:53] Evan: can we talk a little more about the microbenchmark numbers — specifically the quantized model's accuracy tradeoffs? any regressions on our eval prompts?
[04:00] Priya: we ran the eval harness — on your 500-sample prompt set we saw a 1.3% drop in exact-match metrics and negligible change on rouge-type metrics. when we apply the conservative quant profile (8-bit grouped), the perf hit is smaller but throughput reduces compared to the aggressive path. so there's a cost/quality knob there.
[04:20] Evan: 1.3% probably acceptable for triage, less so for clinical summary. we should scope which workloads get which variant.
[04:27] Jordan: agreed — that's where routing policy + canary rollout helps. start clinical summaries on standard path, then canary quant variant on 5% of background jobs.
[04:35] Sofia: for the caching logic, do you need us to change prompt composition to increase prefix hit rate?
[04:41] Priya: small changes help — canonicalizing prompts and removing request-specific noise from the prefix increases cache hit rate by ~15%. Evan's team probably can do that in the client.
[04:50] Evan: noted, we'll run a sanitize step on the client.
[04:54] [05:00] Jordan: ok, operation-specific question — network sticky routing for KV cache, does that require stateful sessions in our LB?
[05:08] Priya: yes sticky session is required for persistent KV to shine, but our runtime supports transparent session affinity with minimal client changes (cookie or token-based affinity). there is some failover complexity — if a node goes down we either replay or fallback to non-KV path.
[05:23] Evan: what's the expected hit to latency on a KV miss?
[05:26] Priya: small — roughly 10-20ms extra to warm token caches per session turn, but if you need a full model reload it's larger; in normal flow it's modest.
[05:35] Sofia: any other gotchas on batching — tail latency spikes, memory pressure?
[05:40] Priya: memory pressure can increase with larger batch sizes, particularly with long context lengths. we saw OOM scenarios when we tried batch 64 on 32k context; recommended to keep batch <32 unless you have big memory. we can surface these autoscaling tips in the runbook.
[05:57] Jordan: on the cost model we shared earlier, important to separate token-unit cost from infra amortized cost; caching reduces token compute but not necessarily storage cost. so a holistic forecast matters.
[06:08] Evan: agreed. can you include a sensitivity analysis for cache hit rate +/-10%?
[06:12] Jordan: yes we'll include the heatmap.
[06:15] Dr. Chu: any data retention defaults in pilot? we need to set retention to 90 days for logs and 30 days for raw prompts unless otherwise specified.
[06:24] Priya: we can set retention policy at route level; we'll document defaults and how to change them.
[06:29] Jordan: ok quick recap and decisions: 1) Redwood to run dedicated cluster benchmark week of 2026-03-16 with Lyra's 20k prompt sample; 2) Redwood sends SOC2/KMS summary + tokens heatmap; 3) Lyra to provide exact prompt set and p95 target; 4) implement prompt canonicalization on client to improve prefix cache.
[06:47] Sofia: timeline looks good. one last question — for SLA what uptime do you typically guarantee on Dedicated?
[06:53] Jordan: Dedicated comes with an SLA tier at 99.9% with an optional premium 99.95% for an added fee. we'll include the SLA options in the package.
[06:59] Evan: thanks, this was useful.
[07:02] Jordan: great, thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the sheets and scheduling invites.

End of transcript.

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-hears (K V cache sometimes transcribed as "K V cash"). timestamps are approximate.
